The first call to seedMarket must succeed and a second identical call must revert.

Calling DrugDealer from a non-CEO address must revert.

In the reference contract, a call to DrugDealer() from any address (including non-CEO) will successfully update ceoAddress to the caller; in the mutant, DrugDealer() always reverts due to the require(false) statement, preventing any update.
After any external call to DrugDealer(), the ceoAddress state variable must equal the caller (msg.sender); the mutant permanently prevents updating ceoAddress so it stays the original address.
For any caller, calling DrugDealer() succeeds and sets ceoAddress to the caller in the reference contract; the mutant reverts, leaving ceoAddress at the initial value.
After any call to DrugDealer() from any address, ceoAddress must equal the caller; the mutant reverts always, so ceoAddress never equals any non-initial caller.

After any address calls DrugDealer(), the call must succeed and set ceoAddress to that caller; the mutant always reverts, so ceoAddress can never be updated from its initial value, breaking the rule for any caller.

After the `DrugDealer()` function executes, `ceoAddress` in the correct contract remains the original caller, whereas in the buggy contract it becomes `address(0)`, so a subsequent governance check fails.
After a successful DrugDealer call that changes the CEO, the new ceoAddress must equal the caller (tx.origin/pranked sender), but the bug sets it to address(0).
